chapter.heading: The Prophet’s Anguish and Hope
chapter.v:
I am
the man who has seen affliction by the rod of His wrath. [Ps. 2:2; Mark 15:1; Luke 22:66; 23:1; John 18:28]

He has
led me and made me walkIn darkness and not in light. [Matt. 20:19; Luke 18:32; Acts]

Surely He
has turned His hand against meTime and time again throughout the day. [Matt. 26:14] [Matt. 26:15]

He has
aged my flesh and my skin,And broken my bones.

He has
besieged meAnd surrounded me with bitterness and woe.

He has
set me in dark placesLike the dead of long ago.

He has
hedged me in so that I cannot get out;He has made my chain heavy.

Even when
I cry and shout,He shuts out my prayer. [Acts 1:19]

He has
blocked my ways with hewn stone;He has made my paths crooked. [Zech. 11:12 #]

He has
been to me a bear lying in wait,Like a lion in ambush. [Jer. 32:6-9; Zech. 11:12, 13 #]

He has
turned aside my ways and torn me in pieces;He has made me desolate. [Mark 15:2-5; Luke 23:2, 3; John 18:29-38 j John 18:37; 1 Tim. 6:13]

He has
bent His bowAnd set me up as a target for the arrow. [Ps. 38:13, 14; Matt. 26:63; John]

He has
caused the arrows of His quiverTo pierce my loins. [Matt. 26:62; John 19:10]

I have
become the ridicule of all my people—Their taunting song all the day.

He has
filled me with bitterness,He has made me drink wormwood. [Mark 15:6-15; Luke 23:17-25; John 18:39–19:16]

He has
also broken my teeth with gravel,And covered me with ashes.

You have
moved my soul far from peace;I have forgotten prosperity.

And I
said, “My strength and my hopeHave perished from the Lord.” [Matt. 21:38; [John 15:22-25]]

Remember my
affliction and roaming,The wormwood and the gall.

My soul
still remembersAnd sinks within me. [Mark 15:11; Luke 23:18; John 18:40; Acts 3:14]

This I
recall to my mind,Therefore I have hope. [Acts 3:14]

Through the
Lord’s mercies we are not consumed,Because His compassions fail not.

They are
new every morning;Great is Your faithfulness.

“The Lord
is my portion,” says my soul,“Therefore I hope in Him!” [Deut. 21:6-8]

The Lord
is good to those who wait for Him,To the soul who seeks Him. [Deut. 19:10; Josh. 2:19;]

It is
good that one should hope and wait quietlyFor the salvation of the Lord. [[Is. 50:6; 53:5] #; Matt. 20:19; Mark 15:15; Luke 23:16, 24, 25; John 19:1,]

It is
good for a man to bearThe yoke in his youth. [Mark 15:16- 20; John 19:2]

Let him
put his mouth in the dust—There may yet be hope. [Ps. 69:19; Is. 53:3 #; Matt. 20:19; Mark 10:34;]

Let him
give his cheek to the one who strikes him,And be full of reproach. [Is. 50:6 #; 52:14; Mic. 5:1; Matt. 26:67; Mark]

For the
Lord will not cast off forever. [Is. 53:7; Matt.]

Though He
causes grief,Yet He will show compassionAccording to the multitude of His mercies. [1 Kin. 21:13; Acts 7:58; Heb. 13:12 b Mark 15:21; Luke 23:26; John 19:17]

For He
does not afflict willingly,Nor grieve the children of men. [Mark 15:22- 32; Luke 23:33-43; John 19:17]

To crush
under one’s feetAll the prisoners of the earth, [Ps. 69:21 #; Matt. 27:48 Mark 15:23-32; Luke 23:33-43; John 19:18-24]

To turn
aside the justice due a manBefore the face of the Most High, [Ps. 22:18 # 1 NU, M omit the rest of v. 35. 36 g Ps. 22:17; Matt. 27:54 #] [Mark 15:24; Luke 23:34; John 19:24]

Or subvert
a man in his cause—The Lord does not approve.

Who is
he who speaks and it comes to pass,When the Lord has not commanded it? [Mark 15:26; Luke 23:38; John 19:19]

Is it
not from the mouth of the Most HighThat woe and well-being proceed?

Why should
a living man complain,A man for the punishment of his sins? [Job 16:4; Ps. Lam. 2:15; Mark 15:29; Luke 23:35]

Let us
lift our hearts and handsTo God in heaven.

We have
transgressed and rebelled;You have not pardoned. [[Matt. 18:11; John 3:14, 15]]

You have
covered Yourself with angerAnd pursued us;You have slain and not pitied. [Ps. 22:8 $]

You have
covered Yourself with a cloud,That prayer should not pass through. [Mark 15:32; Luke 23:39-43]

You have
made us an offscouring and refuseIn the midst of the peoples. [Amos 8:9; Mark 15:33-41; Luke 23:44-49]

All our
enemiesHave opened their mouths against us. [Ps. 22:1 #] [[Heb. 5:7]]

Fear and
a snare have come upon us,Desolation and destruction.

My eyes
overflow with rivers of waterFor the destruction of the daughter of my people. [Ps. 69:21; Mark 15:36; Luke 23:36; John 19:29]

My eyes
flow and do not cease,Without interruption,

Till the
Lord from heavenLooks down and sees. [Mark 15:37; Luke 23:46; John 19:30 u Dan. 9:26; Zech. 11:10, 11; Matt. 17:23; [John 10:18; 1 Cor. 15:3]]

My eyes
bring suffering to my soulBecause of all the daughters of my city. [Ex. 26:31; 2 Chr. 3:14; Zech. 11:10 #; Mark 15:38; Luke 23:45; Heb. 9:3]

My enemies
without causeHunted me down like a bird.

They silenced
my life in the pitAnd threw stones at me.

The waters
flowed over my head;I said, “I am cut off!” [Mark 15:39; Luke 23:47 x Matt.]

I called
on Your name, O Lord,From the lowest pit. [Mark 15:41; Luke 8:2,]

You have
heard my voice:“Do not hide Your earFrom my sighing, from my cry for help.”

You drew
near on the day I called on You,And said, “Do not fear!”

O Lord,
You have pleaded the case for my soul;You have redeemed my life.

O Lord,
You have seen how I am wronged;Judge my case.

You have
seen all their vengeance,All their schemes against me. [Is. 53:9 #; Matt. 26:12]

You have
heard their reproach, O Lord,All their schemes against me,

The lips
of my enemiesAnd their whispering against me all the day.

Look at
their sitting down and their rising up;I am their taunting song. [Matt. 16:21; Mark 8:31; 10:34; Luke 9:22; 13:33; 24:6, 7; John 2:19]

Repay them,
O Lord,According to the work of their hands.

Give them
a veiled heart;Your curse be upon them!

In Your
anger,Pursue and destroy themFrom under the heavens of the Lord. [Dan. 6:17]
